terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Build all three .cpp files into one program here and run it.

tasks.title: Price a repair in price.cpp
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1` in `src/price.cpp`, write `repairPrice` exactly as `src/repair.h` declares it: it takes a repair as a reference to a `const Repair` and gives back a `double`. Ambrose charges 48 for every hour at the bench, counted by the minute, plus the parts: 75 minutes with 18.5 of parts comes to 78.5.

Check builds its own program, which includes `repair.h`, together with your `price.cpp`, calls `repairPrice` with repairs of its own and reads what it gives back.
nextSteps: Copy the first line of `repairPrice` from `repair.h`, without its semicolon.
Give it a body that works out the time at the bench from the minutes.
Add the parts, and give the price back.
Build all three files with the terminal's command.
hints: `price.cpp` already includes `repair.h`, so it knows `Repair`. The first line of the function is the declaration's, with a body in place of the semicolon.
Two whole numbers divided give a whole number, so `minutes / 60` loses the minutes past the hour. Work with `48.0` to keep them.
The shape is `double repairPrice(const Repair& repair) { return repair.minutes * 48.0 / 60 + repair.parts; }`.

tasks.title: Write the pickup line in counter.cpp
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2` in `src/counter.cpp`, write `pickupLine` exactly as `src/repair.h` declares it: it takes a repair as a reference to a `const Repair` and gives back a `std::string`: `Ticket `, the ticket, `: `, the item and ` is ready`. Like this:

```
Ticket 3101: mantel clock is ready
```

Check builds its own program, which includes `repair.h`, together with your `counter.cpp`, calls `pickupLine` with repairs of its own and reads what it gives back.
nextSteps: Copy the first line of `pickupLine` from `repair.h`, without its semicolon.
Join the words, the ticket turned into text, and the item.
Build all three files and run the program.
hints: `counter.cpp` uses the same `Repair` as `price.cpp`, from the same header: a struct can be in every file that includes it.
`std::to_string` turns the ticket into text before it is joined.
The shape is `return "Ticket " + std::to_string(repair.ticket) + ": " + repair.item + " is ready";`.

tasks.title: Add up the day in main.cpp
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3` in `src/main.cpp`, write a function called `dayTotal` that takes the day's repairs as a reference to a `const std::vector<Repair>` and gives back what they come to together, as a `double`, with the price of each one worked out by `repairPrice` from `price.cpp`.

Check builds your `main.cpp` with a `repairPrice` and a `main` of its own, calls `dayTotal` with days of its own, an empty one included, and reads what it gives back. It also counts the calls to `repairPrice`, so this task is judged on its own whatever Task 1 does.
nextSteps: Write the first line: a `const std::vector<Repair>&` in, a `double` back.
Start a total at 0, and go through the repairs.
Add what `repairPrice` gives back for each one.
In `main`, print the total of `today`, then build all three files.
hints: `main.cpp` includes `repair.h`, so it can call `repairPrice` though its body is in another file. The linker joins the two once both files are on the command line.
Call `repairPrice(repair)` for each repair and add what it gives back: the price is worked out in one place only.
The shape is `double total = 0; for (const auto& repair : repairs) { total += repairPrice(repair); } return total;`.
